stateEligibility.intro: TeleDirectMD sees adults 18 and older who are physically located in New York State during the video visit. The state's telehealth law, Public Health Law Article 29-G, defines telehealth as the use of electronic information and communication technologies to deliver health care services, including assessment, diagnosis, consultation and treatment. What matters for eligibility is where you are when the visit happens. A visitor in a Manhattan hotel or a student on a semester in Ithaca can be seen. A resident on a trip to a state TeleDirectMD does not serve cannot be seen until they are back in New York or in another served state.
localTriggers: You must be physically in New York State at the time of the visit. Your home address, driver's license state and insurance do not change this.
Visitors count. New York City drew 65 million visitors in 2025 (NYC Tourism + Conventions); a visitor physically in New York during the visit is eligible like any adult resident.
Commuters should check where they will be during the visit: a patient in New Jersey or Connecticut at visit time is seen under that state's rules, not New York's.
Adults 18 and older only. TeleDirectMD does not see children in New York or anywhere else.

stateTreatmentContext.pharmacyAndRx: New York requires prescriptions to be transmitted electronically from prescriber to pharmacy (Public Health Law Section 281; the state Department of Health has enforced the mandate for controlled and non-controlled prescriptions since March 27, 2016). When a prescription is appropriate, it goes straight to the pharmacy you choose: a CVS, Walgreens or Duane Reade in the city, a Wegmans or Kinney Drugs pharmacy upstate, a Walmart pharmacy, or an independent pharmacy near you. A pharmacy here can dispense only on a prescription from a person legally authorized to issue it (Education Law Section 6810), so a visitor's home-country prescription cannot be filled in New York; a New York-licensed physician who evaluates you can decide whether a new prescription is appropriate. TeleDirectMD does not prescribe controlled substances in any state.

stateEpidemiology.general: New York's seasons shape what brings adults to a visit. Flu activity usually builds through December; the state Department of Health formally declared influenza prevalent on December 2, 2025, December 18, 2024 and December 6, 2023, and TeleDirectMD's FluHub tracks the state's flu activity weekly. Tick-borne disease is concentrated outside New York City: the Department of Health's 2025 tick-borne disease report names the Capital District as the region with the highest incidence of Lyme disease, anaplasmosis and babesiosis for 2020 to 2024, with high counts on Long Island and in the Hudson Valley, and adult blacklegged ticks stay active into the fall. The city's density and visitor volume mean respiratory and sexually transmitted infections spread quickly, which is why both the state and the city publish their own clinical guidance on doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis. This context is for awareness only and is not a substitute for an individual evaluation.

uti-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: For women in New York with typical, uncomplicated bladder infection symptoms (burning, frequency, urgency), a video visit is often enough to decide on treatment. The New York State Department of Health's adult outpatient treatment recommendations note that cloudy or foul-smelling urine alone does not diagnose a UTI, and that treating bacteria found in urine without symptoms is not recommended for healthy adults. TeleDirectMD's UTI care is limited to non-pregnant adult women; men with urinary symptoms, and anyone with fever, flank pain, vomiting or pregnancy, should be seen in person. When an antibiotic is appropriate, it is sent electronically to the pharmacy you choose. Flat $79 for adults physically in New York.

sectionNotes.medications: New York City's Health Department publishes a citywide antibiogram each year, pooling hospital lab results so clinicians can see local antibiotic resistance. In the 2024 edition, only 65 percent of E. coli urine samples from emergency departments were susceptible to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, while 98 percent were susceptible to nitrofurantoin and 95 percent to fosfomycin. That resistance is far above the 20 percent level the table above uses for trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, so for patients in New York City, nitrofurantoin or fosfomycin come first, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is used only when a culture has shown the bacteria are susceptible to it. Emergency department samples tend to be more resistant than simple bladder infections treated outside the hospital, so the true community rate is probably lower, and the data do not describe upstate New York.
sectionNotes.differential: Chlamydia can cause burning that feels like a bladder infection. The New York City Health Department lists pain during urination and vaginal discharge that is different than usual among its symptoms, and notes that most people with chlamydia have none at all. In the city's 2024 surveillance report, women ages 15 to 24 accounted for 56 percent of chlamydia cases reported among women, with a case rate about five times that of women overall.
sectionNotes.when-not: Men with urinary burning are referred to in-person care rather than treated for a UTI here. The New York City Health Department notes that burning or pain during urination, sometimes with discharge from the penis, can be urethritis, which can be a sign of a sexually transmitted infection such as chlamydia or gonorrhea. In New York City, the Health Department's Sexual Health Clinics provide low- or no-cost STI care to anyone 12 or older, mostly on a walk-in basis and regardless of immigration status, and they still see patients who cannot pay the sliding-scale fee.

faqs.question: Where can I get an STI test in New York City if my symptoms might not be a UTI?
faqs.answer: If you have symptoms, the New York City Health Department's Sexual Health Clinics see patients 12 and older, mostly walk-in, at low or no cost. For routine testing without symptoms, the Chelsea Express Clinic in Manhattan and the Fort Greene Express Clinic in Brooklyn offer appointments for HIV, chlamydia, gonorrhea and syphilis testing, with chlamydia and gonorrhea results usually available within hours. The clinic hotline is 347-396-7959, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

sore-throat-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Sore throats peak in New York in late fall and winter; searches for strep throat across the state run about 40,000 a month in November and December. Most adult sore throats are viral, and the 2025 IDSA strep guideline estimates group A strep at 5 to 15 percent of adult cases, so the key question is whether you need a strep test. A video visit can sort out who needs testing and who does not, and can point you to a nearby pharmacy or urgent care for a swab when one is needed. Flat $79 for adults physically in New York.

sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: The state Department of Health says the bacteria spread by direct contact with nose and throat discharges of an infected person. If someone in your household has been diagnosed with strep throat, mention it during your visit, since close contact is one of the risk factors listed above.
sectionNotes.symptoms-redflags: Group A strep occasionally causes invasive infection. The state Department of Health lists fever, dizziness, confusion, low blood pressure, rash and abdominal pain as early signs of streptococcal toxic shock syndrome. Those signs need emergency care, not a video visit.
sectionNotes.differential: A video visit cannot swab your throat, so it helps to know what New York pharmacies can and cannot test. State law lets pharmacists order and administer FDA-authorized COVID-19 and influenza tests (Education Law Section 6801), which can help when a sore throat comes with flu or COVID-19 symptoms. Strep tests are not on that list. A 2025 Assembly bill (A3285) would add tests for strep throat; it was referred to the Assembly Higher Education Committee on January 7, 2026, and has not become law.
sectionNotes.home-care: Strep throat stops being contagious sooner than many people expect. The New York State Department of Health says treatment with an appropriate antibiotic for 24 hours or longer eliminates contagiousness. If you need time off before then, New York's paid sick leave law (Labor Law Section 196-b) covers your own illness and its diagnosis, care or treatment, and New York City employers can require documentation only after more than three consecutive workdays of protected time off.

faqs.question: Can I get a strep test at a pharmacy in New York?
faqs.answer: New York's pharmacist testing law names FDA-authorized COVID-19 and influenza tests and does not list strep tests (Education Law Section 6801). A bill to add strep throat testing, Assembly bill A3285, was referred to committee on January 7, 2026 and has not become law. If Dr. Bhavsar decides during a video visit that a strep test would change your treatment, the visit can point you to a nearby place for a swab.

faqs.question: When can I go back to work with strep throat in New York?
faqs.answer: The New York State Department of Health says treatment with an appropriate antibiotic for 24 hours or longer eliminates contagiousness. You may still feel too sick to work. State paid sick leave covers your own illness, and in New York City an employer can require documentation only after more than three consecutive workdays of protected time off.

faqs.question: When is strep season in New York?
faqs.answer: A 2023 advisory from the state and city health departments describes a seasonal pattern for group A strep infections from December through April, and notes that strep throat is most common among children ages 5 to 15. Most adult sore throats are still viral. If your sore throat comes with signs the state lists for streptococcal toxic shock syndrome, such as fever with dizziness, confusion, a rash or abdominal pain, seek emergency care.

influenza-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Flu activity in New York usually builds through December; the state Department of Health declared influenza prevalent on December 2, 2025, December 18, 2024 and December 6, 2023. Antiviral treatment works best when started early, ideally within 48 hours of symptoms, and matters most for adults at higher risk. A same-day video visit for adults physically in New York can decide whether an antiviral is appropriate and send it to your pharmacy. For what is circulating now, the Department of Health's New York State Flu Tracker posts lab-confirmed flu cases and hospitalizations by county every Friday from October through May, and TeleDirectMD's FluHub charts the state's weekly activity against past seasons. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.what-is: The 2025-26 season set a New York record. The state Department of Health reported 71,123 positive flu cases in the seven days ending December 20, 2025, the most it had recorded in one week since flu became reportable in 2004, and a 38 percent rise over the week before. Flu hospitalizations climbed from 2,251 to 3,666 that week. By the week ending May 23, 2026, the season totals stood at 445,545 laboratory-confirmed flu cases and 26,545 flu hospitalizations. New York requires laboratory-confirmed flu to be reported to public health, which is what these totals count.
sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Skipping the flu shot is a risk factor you can still fix mid-season in New York: the state Department of Health says the vaccine is available to New Yorkers ages 2 and older at participating pharmacies without a prescription. If you work in a hospital, nursing home or home care agency, the season also changes your workday. Once the Health Commissioner declares influenza prevalent, staff who are not vaccinated for the current season must wear a surgical or procedure mask where patients or residents may be present (10 NYCRR 2.59). For 2025-26, that rule lifted when influenza was declared no longer prevalent on April 23, 2026.
sectionNotes.differential: The state declared influenza no longer prevalent on April 23, 2026, yet in the week ending May 23, 2026, influenza B made up 84 percent of positive flu cases in the state's weekly report. If you want to know whether it is flu or COVID-19, New York law lets pharmacists order and administer FDA-authorized COVID-19 and influenza tests (Education Law Section 6801), so ask your pharmacy whether it offers them. A negative rapid flu test does not rule out flu, according to NYC Health Department clinical guidance.
sectionNotes.treatment-options: New York's health departments frame antivirals around risk. The state Department of Health says flu is treatable for high-risk people with antiviral medicine if taken within 48 hours of symptoms. The NYC Health Department's clinical guidance adds that adults with mild flu-like illness who are not at high risk usually do not require an antiviral, though clinicians may prescribe one to reduce the number of days of symptoms. In a video visit, Dr. Bhavsar weighs your timing, symptoms and health history to decide whether an antiviral is appropriate for you.
sectionNotes.medications: Two New York pharmacy rules can help with the cost of a flu prescription. Under Education Law Section 6816-a, a pharmacist substitutes a less expensive drug product with the same active ingredients, dosage form and strength as the drug prescribed, when the substitute is on the state's approved list and the prescriber does not prohibit substitution. And every New York pharmacy that sells drugs at retail must make a drug retail price list available and display a sign reading "Drug Retail Price List Available Upon Request," so you can ask about prices before you choose the pharmacy that receives your prescription.
sectionNotes.home-care: Staying home while you are contagious is protected in New York. State law gives employees up to 40 hours of paid sick leave a year at employers with 5 to 99 workers and up to 56 hours at employers with 100 or more, and the leave covers your own illness and its diagnosis, care or treatment (Labor Law Section 196-b). In New York City, an employer can require documentation only after you use more than three consecutive workdays of protected time off, and cannot require the reason for the leave to be disclosed.

faqs.question: Do I need a flu test before getting flu treatment in New York?
faqs.answer: Not usually. NYC Health Department clinical guidance says testing is generally not necessary for most patients with mild influenza-like illness, that rapid test kits have poor sensitivity, and that a negative result should not be used to rule out flu. If a test would help, New York law allows pharmacists to order and administer FDA-authorized flu and COVID-19 tests, so ask your pharmacy whether it offers them. In a video visit, Dr. Bhavsar can decide whether a test would change your treatment.

faqs.question: Can my employer in New York ask for a doctor's note when I miss work with the flu?
faqs.answer: In New York City, an employer may require documentation only after you use more than three consecutive workdays of protected time off, cannot require you or the person providing it to disclose the reason, and must reimburse you if your health care provider charges a fee for it. Statewide, Labor Law Section 196-b bars employers from requiring disclosure of confidential information about a mental or physical illness as a condition of providing sick leave.

faqs.question: How big was the 2025-26 flu season in New York?
faqs.answer: It was the largest on record for a single week. The state Department of Health reported 71,123 positive flu cases in the week ending December 20, 2025, the most recorded in one week since flu became reportable in 2004, and 445,545 laboratory-confirmed cases with 26,545 flu hospitalizations for the season through May 23, 2026. In New York City alone, the Health Department reported more than 146,000 positive flu cases by February 12, 2026.

covid-19-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: For adults in New York with a positive COVID-19 test and mild to moderate symptoms, timing matters: oral antivirals are started within the first days of symptoms, and some interact with common medicines, so a medication review is part of the visit. A video visit for adults physically in New York can review your test, symptoms and medication list, and when treatment is appropriate send a prescription electronically to a New York pharmacy. Trouble breathing or chest pain needs 911, not a video visit. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.what-is: In New York's 2025-26 respiratory season, the state Department of Health counted 110,470 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 cases and 12,634 COVID-19 hospitalizations through the week ending May 23, 2026. By late May, the state's weekly report described COVID-19 activity as sporadic, which it defines as small numbers of lab-confirmed cases.
sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: The New York State Department of Health's list of people at higher risk from COVID-19 names some groups the shared list above does not: people who are pregnant or were recently pregnant, people with a disability, and people who smoke now or used to smoke. It also notes that risk rises sharply after age 75, that the list is not complete, and that having more than one risk factor raises your risk more. If you are healthy and none apply, the Department says national expert guidelines do not recommend routine antiviral treatment.
sectionNotes.differential: Because COVID-19 and flu overlap so much, a test can help sort them out. New York law lets pharmacists order and administer FDA-authorized COVID-19 and influenza tests (Education Law Section 6801), so ask your pharmacy whether it offers them. The state Department of Health also tests wastewater for the virus that causes COVID-19 to follow community trends, but it says wastewater data is not a substitute for people getting tested.
sectionNotes.treatment-options: In New York, more than one kind of clinician can start COVID-19 treatment. The state Department of Health says a pharmacist in New York may prescribe Paxlovid directly under the federal PREP Act and FDA Emergency Use Authorization, an authority it says is due to end on June 29, 2027, and that many practices offer same-day telehealth visits for this. It also says COVID-19 medicines are available at pharmacies throughout New York State. A video visit with Dr. Bhavsar includes the medication and health history review that decides whether Paxlovid is appropriate for you.
sectionNotes.home-care: The NYC Health Department says you can leave home and resume work or school once you have had no fever for 24 hours without fever-reducing medicine and your other COVID-19 symptoms are getting better. For the next 5 days, it advises extra precautions, including a well-fitting mask that covers your nose and mouth whenever you are around other people. Its guidance for clinicians also notes that COVID-19 rebound is generally mild and does not represent a treatment failure or resistance.

faqs.question: Can a pharmacist in New York prescribe Paxlovid?
faqs.answer: For now, yes. The New York State Department of Health says a pharmacist in New York may prescribe Paxlovid directly under the federal PREP Act and FDA Emergency Use Authorization, which it says is due to end on June 29, 2027, after which pharmacists will no longer be able to prescribe it. A physician visit is another route: by video, Dr. Bhavsar can review your test, symptoms, kidney and liver history and medication list, and send a prescription when appropriate.

faqs.question: Does New York still have a separate COVID-19 paid sick leave law?
faqs.answer: No. The state's Paid Family Leave program lists July 31, 2025 as the date New York's COVID-19 paid leave law expires.

faqs.question: When can I go back to work after COVID-19 in New York City?
faqs.answer: NYC Health Department guidance says you can return to work or school when you have had no fever for 24 hours without fever-reducing medicine and your other symptoms are getting better, then take extra precautions, including a mask around other people, for 5 days. Under the city's sick leave law, your employer can require documentation only after more than three consecutive workdays of protected time off, and cannot require the reason to be disclosed.

sinus-infection-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Most sinus infections in New York adults start as colds and clear without antibiotics. A video visit helps separate those from the smaller group that meets guideline criteria for a bacterial sinus infection: symptoms lasting 10 days or more without improvement, or getting worse again after starting to improve. For adults physically in New York, Dr. Bhavsar can review your timeline, suggest what helps at home, and send a prescription to a New York pharmacy when one is appropriate. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Allergic rhinitis, one of the risk factors above, follows a predictable calendar in New York City. A March 2026 NYC Health Department advisory says over-the-counter allergy medication sales typically rise in April and May, when tree pollen from trees such as maple, birch and oak peaks; grass pollen starts in late spring and peaks in summer; and ragweed and mold spores bother people mainly in late summer and fall. The same advisory says evidence points to longer pollen seasons and more pollen production due to climate change.
sectionNotes.differential: Wildfire smoke is a New York look-alike for sinus trouble. On July 15, 2026, the state issued a statewide Air Quality Health Advisory for fine particles from Canadian wildfire smoke, with air forecast as unhealthy in the Eastern Lake Ontario, Central New York and Western New York regions. The state Department of Environmental Conservation says exposure can cause short-term irritation of the eyes, nose and throat, along with coughing, sneezing and a runny nose. If your congestion began on a smoke day or a high-pollen day, tell Dr. Bhavsar during the visit.
sectionNotes.home-care: For allergy-driven congestion, the NYC Health Department's 2026 pollen advisory says a simple nasal saline spray is best to relieve congestion and flush out allergens. It also advises that allergy medications such as oral antihistamines and intranasal corticosteroids be started at least several weeks before symptoms begin. On air quality alert days, the state advises avoiding strenuous activity where fine particle levels are high.
sectionNotes.medications: Two New York pharmacy rules can lower what you pay for a sinus prescription. Under Education Law Section 6816-a, a pharmacist substitutes a less expensive drug product with the same active ingredients, dosage form and strength as the drug prescribed, when the substitute is on the state's approved list and the prescriber does not prohibit substitution. Every New York pharmacy that sells drugs at retail must also make a drug retail price list available and display a sign reading "Drug Retail Price List Available Upon Request," so you can ask about prices before choosing where your prescription is sent.

faqs.question: Is it a sinus infection or seasonal allergies in New York?
faqs.answer: Timing is one clue. The NYC Health Department says tree pollen peaks in April and May, grass pollen peaks in summer, and ragweed and mold spores bother people mainly in late summer and fall. Symptoms lasting 10 days or more without improvement, or worsening after starting to improve, fit the guideline criteria for a bacterial sinus infection. A video visit can sort out which pattern fits you.

faqs.question: How can I find out about air quality alerts in New York?
faqs.answer: The state Department of Environmental Conservation issues Air Quality Health Advisories when pollution is expected to exceed an Air Quality Index value of 100. It runs a toll-free Air Quality Hotline at 1-800-535-1345, and you can sign up with the department to receive Air Quality Alerts. On alert days, the state advises avoiding strenuous activity in areas where fine particle levels are high.

tick-bite-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Tick bites are a real concern across much of New York outside the city. The New York State Department of Health's 2025 tick-borne disease report names the Capital District as the region with the highest incidence of Lyme disease, anaplasmosis and babesiosis for 2020 to 2024, with high counts on Long Island and in the Hudson Valley, and adult blacklegged ticks stay active into the fall. A video visit for adults in New York can go over how long the tick was attached and where you were, decide whether a single dose of preventive antibiotic is appropriate, and explain what rash or fever to watch for. Flat $79.

what-is: New York reports tick-borne illness in large numbers. Outside New York City, the state Department of Health counted 18,704 confirmed or probable Lyme disease cases in 2024, plus 1,960 anaplasmosis, 670 babesiosis and 110 ehrlichiosis cases. Part of the recent rise in Lyme counts reflects the 2022 national case definition, under which a positive laboratory result alone can classify a case.

New York City reports separately. Preliminary 2025 city data show 2,928 Lyme disease, 107 anaplasmosis, 98 babesiosis and 25 ehrlichiosis cases among residents, and most of those people reported travel outside the city during the exposure period.
sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Where you were matters. In New York City, the Health Department finds blacklegged ticks, the species that carries Lyme disease, on Staten Island and in focal areas of the Bronx (Pelham Bay Park and Hunter Island), and 30 to 50 percent of the ticks it tests carry the Lyme bacterium. Local transmission is reported on Staten Island and, rarely, in the Bronx. Lone star ticks are found on Staten Island and rarely in Queens. Outside the city, the state's tick surveillance found blacklegged tick nymphs at their highest average density in its Metropolitan Area region from 2020 to 2024.
sectionNotes.symptoms-redflags: Two New York tick problems sit outside the usual Lyme checklist. Alpha-gal syndrome, linked mainly to lone star tick bites, is an allergy to the alpha-gal molecule found in meat and other mammal products, with symptoms about 2 to 6 hours after eating or exposure; New York City began laboratory-based reporting in 2024 and received over 140 reports in 2025. Hives, swelling or trouble breathing hours after a meal need in-person care, and trouble breathing needs 911. Powassan virus is rare here, with fewer than 10 cases a year outside the city from 2020 to 2024, but in 2024 the state found it in adult blacklegged ticks in its Metropolitan Area and Capital District regions.
sectionNotes.treatment-options: The New York City Health Department's 2026 advisory to clinicians says a single dose of doxycycline may be used to reduce the risk of Lyme disease for people bitten in a highly endemic area, and it names Staten Island and the surrounding northeastern states. The other conditions on this page still apply: a blacklegged tick, a long enough attachment, and a visit within 72 hours of removing it.
sectionNotes.medications: Single-dose doxycycline is aimed at Lyme disease only. The New York City Health Department notes that prophylaxis has not been shown to prevent other tick-borne diseases, and that matters in New York, where anaplasmosis and babesiosis were reported in the hundreds to thousands in 2024 and the state finds the babesiosis parasite more often in ticks from its Metropolitan Area region than elsewhere. Fever, chills or body aches in the weeks after a New York tick bite still need an in-person exam and blood work, even if you took the preventive dose.
sectionNotes.home-care: Do not count on winter to end tick season. The state Department of Health says blacklegged ticks are most active when temperatures are above freezing, and that ticks can be found in most areas of New York. The state parks office warns that tick-borne illness is a particular concern in areas with tall grass or dense vegetation just off the trail. The Department publishes current and past tick collection and testing results on Health Data NY, along with a Tick Score map of the chance of meeting an infected blacklegged tick in each region of the state.

faqs.question: Can I get Lyme disease from a tick bite in New York City?
faqs.answer: Yes, though most city residents with Lyme disease were infected elsewhere. The city Health Department reports local transmission of tick-borne disease on Staten Island and, rarely, in the Bronx, where blacklegged ticks live in Pelham Bay Park and on Hunter Island. In 2025, most of the 2,928 city residents with Lyme disease reported travel outside New York City during the exposure period, often to upstate New York, Long Island or elsewhere in the Northeast.

faqs.question: Does a tick bite from Staten Island count for preventive doxycycline?
faqs.answer: It can. The New York City Health Department's 2026 clinician advisory names Staten Island as a highly endemic area where a single preventive dose of doxycycline may be used to reduce the risk of Lyme disease. The usual conditions still apply: the tick should be a blacklegged tick, attached long enough, and removed within the past 72 hours. A video visit can review a photo of the tick and decide whether the dose is appropriate.

faqs.question: I found an Asian longhorned tick in New York City. Should I worry?
faqs.answer: The New York City Health Department reports Asian longhorned ticks in all five boroughs and lists no known disease risk to humans in the United States to date. Telling tick species apart from a photo is not always certain, so if you are unsure which tick bit you, or a rash or fever follows, it is worth a visit. Blacklegged and lone star ticks are also found in parts of the city.

chlamydia-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: For adults in New York with a positive chlamydia test, a video visit can confirm the result, prescribe treatment when appropriate and cover retesting and partner notification. Public Health Law Section 2312 allows expedited partner therapy for chlamydia and for other sexually transmitted infections the CDC recommends it for, which lets a clinician provide treatment for a patient's sex partner without a separate exam; whether it fits your situation is decided during the visit. Prescriptions go electronically to the pharmacy you choose. Flat $79, discreet, for adults physically in New York.

sectionNotes.what-is: Chlamydia is the most reported sexually transmitted infection in New York State, according to the state Department of Health's 2023 data. The Department counted 101,520 diagnoses in 2024, 7 percent fewer than in 2023, and New York ranked 10th among all states for total chlamydia cases in 2023. In New York City, the chlamydia rate fell 6.3 percent from 2023 to 2024, but almost all of that drop was among men: the rate fell 12.7 percent among men and only 0.4 percent among women.
sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Age is a clear pattern in New York's data. In the state's 2024 surveillance report, chlamydia rates were highest in people 15 to 29, and rates among females 15 to 24 greatly exceeded those among males the same age. In New York City in 2024, women ages 15 to 24 made up 56 percent of reported cases among women, with a case rate about five times that of women overall. Neighborhood matters too: in 2024, Hunts Point-Mott Haven, Crotona-Tremont and Highbridge-Morrisania in the Bronx were among the city neighborhoods with high chlamydia rates.
sectionNotes.how-it-works: For the testing step, New York City's Health Department runs Express Clinics in Chelsea (Manhattan) and Fort Greene (Brooklyn) that test people without symptoms for HIV, chlamydia, gonorrhea and syphilis by appointment, with chlamydia and gonorrhea results usually available within hours. Its Sexual Health Clinics offer low- or no-cost STI services to anyone 12 or older, regardless of immigration status. Outside the city, the state Department of Health points people to its Provider Directory to find an STI provider.
sectionNotes.treatment-options: Here is how expedited partner therapy works in New York. It covers partners you had sex with in the 60 days before your symptoms or diagnosis, or your most recent partner if there was none in that window. The prescription can be marked "EPT" and filled without your partner's name, address or date of birth. Your partner pays for the medicine, and your insurance cannot be billed for it. Extra pills or refills on your own prescription for a partner are not allowed. EPT is not used if you are known to also have syphilis, or in cases involving abuse.
sectionNotes.home-care: Chlamydia is a reportable disease in New York, and labs report positive results to the health department. Because of that, you may get a call or visit from a health department Partner Services specialist, sometimes before you have talked with your clinician about it. Partner Services is free and confidential: it can help you tell partners, and it will never tell a partner who you are or when you were tested. To confirm a caller is genuine, ask for their supervisor or, in person, for an ID badge. The city Health Department advises retesting three to four months after treatment.
sectionNotes.when-not: If you also need a gonorrhea injection or an in-person exam, New York City's Sexual Health Clinics provide low- or no-cost STI care to anyone 12 or older, mostly walk-in and regardless of immigration status, and they still see patients who cannot pay the sliding-scale fee. The clinic hotline, 347-396-7959, answers Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

faqs.question: Is chlamydia reported to the health department in New York?
faqs.answer: Yes. Chlamydia trachomatis infection is on New York's list of reportable communicable diseases (10 NYCRR Section 2.1), and the New York City Health Code requires it to be reported to the Health Department within 24 hours. Labs that test for STIs must report positive results too. The state says Partner Services gives priority follow-up to certain chlamydia cases, such as pregnant women, and that its help is free and confidential.

faqs.question: Can my partner fill an EPT prescription in New York without giving their name?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under New York's expedited partner therapy law, Public Health Law Section 2312, a pharmacist can fill a prescription marked "EPT" even when the partner's name, address and date of birth are not on it, according to the state AIDS Institute's EPT guidance. The partner pays for the medicine, in cash or with their own insurance; your insurance cannot be billed for it.

faqs.question: What should my partner know before taking EPT medicine for chlamydia?
faqs.answer: New York's guidance says a partner should see a clinician before taking EPT medicine if they are allergic to antibiotics, are or could be pregnant, have abdominal, pelvic or testicular pain, fever, nausea or vomiting, have serious health problems, or take other medicines. It also recommends a full STI check, including an HIV test, even after taking EPT. In New York City, report a bad reaction to EPT by calling 311.

doxypep-sti-prevention-online.stateConditionParagraph: Doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis (doxy-PEP) is a single dose of doxycycline taken within 72 hours after condomless sex to lower the chance of syphilis, gonorrhea and chlamydia. New York was early on it: the New York State Department of Health AIDS Institute published doxy-PEP clinical guidance on September 25, 2023, and the New York City Health Department issued its own provider guidance on November 9, 2023. A video visit for adults physically in the state reviews whether you meet the criteria, the side effects and the testing schedule that goes with it. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.eligibility-checklist: The state AIDS Institute's guideline, updated October 15, 2024, tells clinicians to offer doxy-PEP to cisgender men and transgender women with partners assigned male at birth even without a recent STI if their risk is ongoing, and to consider it case by case for cisgender men with multiple partners assigned female at birth. The state Department of Health also allows case-by-case use for cisgender women, while the New York City Health Department's 2023 provider letter does not recommend it for them. TeleDirectMD's doxy-PEP visit uses the checklist above.
sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Syphilis is a large part of why doxy-PEP matters in New York. The state Department of Health reports that primary and secondary syphilis diagnoses fell 18 percent in 2024, to 2,360, and that 2,002 of them were among males. In 2023, 74 percent of males diagnosed identified as men who have sex with men. In New York City in 2024, Manhattan's Chelsea-Clinton had the highest rates of gonorrhea and early syphilis; Central Harlem-Morningside Heights and Williamsburg-Bushwick were also high for gonorrhea, and Highbridge-Morrisania and East Harlem for early syphilis.
sectionNotes.medications: New York's AIDS Institute guideline recommends a 30- to 90-day supply of doxy-PEP, with the number of pills based on how often you expect to need a dose, and says shared decision-making can settle on the lowest quantity that fits. It also asks clinicians to make sure your STI tests have been done before each refill.
sectionNotes.home-care: New York's follow-up schedule is tighter than the 3-to-6-month range described above. The state AIDS Institute guideline asks clinicians to screen people on doxy-PEP for HIV, chlamydia, gonorrhea and syphilis at least every 3 months, including throat and rectal testing when indicated, to check for hepatitis B when starting and hepatitis C at least once a year. If you are in New York, plan on that testing at least every 3 months for as long as you use doxy-PEP.
sectionNotes.when-not: A possible HIV exposure is an emergency that doxy-PEP does not cover. New York's AIDS Institute guideline says the first dose of HIV PEP should ideally be taken within 2 hours of the exposure and no later than 72 hours. In New York City, call the 24/7 PEP Hotline at 844-3-PEPNYC (844-373-7692), or go to an emergency room, clinic or city Sexual Health Clinic and ask for PEP; when the city clinics are busy, people seeking HIV PEP get priority.

faqs.question: Where else can I get doxy-PEP in New York?
faqs.answer: The New York City Health Department offers doxy PEP at all of its Sexual Health Clinics, and its NYC Health Map now lists other locations that provide it. Outside the city, the state Department of Health points people to the AIDS Institute Provider Directory to find a provider. The city clinics also test for STIs and offer appointments with a trained advisor about HIV PrEP.

faqs.question: I take doxy-PEP and a partner tested positive for chlamydia. Do I need expedited partner therapy?
faqs.answer: Maybe not, according to New York's AIDS Institute EPT guidance. If you took doxy-PEP correctly after every encounter with that partner and have no symptoms, EPT may not be necessary, but you should still get tested, because doxy-PEP is not 100 percent effective, especially against gonorrhea. If you do take EPT doxycycline, do not take a doxy-PEP dose with it: no more than 200 mg of doxycycline in 24 hours.

faqs.question: Does doxy-PEP protect against mpox?
faqs.answer: No. The New York State Department of Health says doxy-PEP does not help prevent HIV, mpox or other viral infections. Mpox has a vaccine: all New York City Sexual Health Clinics offer mpox vaccination as a standalone walk-in service, first and second doses, regardless of insurance or immigration status. The city Health Department stresses getting both doses for maximum protection.

pink-eye-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Pink eye spreads easily in shared New York spaces such as offices, subway cars and dorms, and most cases are viral or allergic rather than bacterial. A video visit lets Dr. Bhavsar look at the eye on camera, ask about discharge, contact lenses and vision changes, and decide whether a prescription eye drop is appropriate. Eye pain, light sensitivity, vision loss or contact lens wear with a red eye need same-day in-person care. Flat $79 for adults physically in New York.

sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Allergic pink eye in New York City tracks the pollen calendar. A March 2026 NYC Health Department advisory on the pollen season, asthma and allergic rhinoconjunctivitis says over-the-counter allergy medication sales typically rise in April and May, when tree pollen peaks, that grass pollen starts in late spring and peaks in summer, and that ragweed and mold spores bother people mainly in late summer and fall. It adds that evidence points to longer pollen seasons and more pollen production due to climate change.
sectionNotes.differential: Wildfire smoke can redden and irritate the eyes without any infection. On July 15, 2026, New York issued a statewide Air Quality Health Advisory for fine particles from Canadian wildfire smoke, and the state Department of Environmental Conservation says exposure can cause short-term irritation of the eyes, nose and throat. If your eyes became red on a smoke day, tell Dr. Bhavsar.
sectionNotes.medications: The NYC Health Department's 2026 pollen advisory recommends artificial tears to help soothe irritated eyes, the same supportive option listed in the table above. It also advises against using any eye product containing a vasoconstrictor, the redness-relief type of drop, for more than 2 to 3 days, to avoid rebound redness and dependency. If you have been using redness-relief drops, mention it during your visit.
sectionNotes.when-not: A chemical splash to the eye needs emergency care, not a video visit. New York's two regional poison control centers answer the national Poison Help line, 1-800-222-1222. The New York City Poison Center serves the five boroughs, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester, and can also be reached at 212-POISONS (212-764-7667); its calls are free, confidential and answered 24/7 by registered pharmacists and nurses certified in poison information, with translation in more than 150 languages. The Upstate New York Poison Center in Syracuse serves every other county.

faqs.question: Who do I call in New York if a chemical gets in my eye?
faqs.answer: Call 911 or go to an emergency department for a chemical exposure to the eye. Poison specialists can also advise by phone at 1-800-222-1222, which reaches the New York City Poison Center for the five boroughs, Long Island and Westchester, and the Upstate New York Poison Center for the rest of the state. In the city, you can also call 212-POISONS (212-764-7667), free and confidential, 24/7.

faqs.question: Can pollen or wildfire smoke make my eyes red in New York?
faqs.answer: Yes. The NYC Health Department describes allergic rhinoconjunctivitis flaring with tree pollen in April and May, grass pollen in summer and ragweed in late summer and fall. The state Department of Environmental Conservation says wildfire smoke, like the Canadian smoke behind New York's July 15, 2026 statewide air quality advisory, can cause short-term irritation of the eyes, nose and throat. A video visit can help tell irritation or allergy apart from infectious pink eye.

faqs.question: Are redness-relief eye drops a good idea for pink eye?
faqs.answer: Only briefly, if at all. The NYC Health Department advises people to avoid any eye product containing a vasoconstrictor for more than 2 to 3 days, to avoid rebound redness and dependency, and recommends artificial tears to soothe irritated eyes. Redness-relief drops do not treat infection. If your eye is red with discharge, pain or vision changes, a video visit can decide the next step.

yeast-infection-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Yeast infection is the most-searched condition in TeleDirectMD's catalog in New York, about 44,000 searches a month across related terms. For adult women in New York with typical symptoms and no red flags, a video visit can confirm whether the picture fits a yeast infection or something that looks similar, such as bacterial vaginosis or trichomoniasis, and send treatment to a New York pharmacy when appropriate. Recurrent infections or pregnancy change the plan and are discussed during the visit. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: The New York City Health Department describes a yeast infection as an overgrowth of yeast that normally lives in the genital area. It notes that yeast infections can pass between sex partners but are not considered a sexually transmitted infection, because they also happen without sex. The Department also advises against douching or cleaning the inside of the vagina with water or other fluids, which it says can change the vagina's natural balance of bacteria and acidity and increase the chance of infections and pelvic inflammatory disease.
sectionNotes.differential: Trichomoniasis is one of the infections that can look like a yeast infection. The New York City Health Department lists itching or irritation in and around the vagina among its symptoms, notes that most people with trichomoniasis have no symptoms at all, and says diagnosis is made by swabbing the vagina and testing the fluid. A swab can also test for a yeast infection. When symptoms do not fit a typical yeast infection, in-person testing is the next step.
sectionNotes.when-not: If you need an in-person swab to tell a yeast infection apart from an STI, New York City's Health Department runs Sexual Health Clinics that provide low- or no-cost STI services to anyone 12 or older, regardless of immigration status, including people who cannot pay the sliding-scale fee. Its hotline, 347-396-7959, also connects callers to a clinic provider by telemedicine for some services, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

faqs.question: Does my partner need treatment for my yeast infection?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The New York City Health Department says sex partners do not need to be treated for yeast infections. Yeast infections can also occur on the penis: the Department lists itching and rash as symptoms there and notes that pills or creams applied to the penis cure it, and that many of these treatments are available without a prescription.

faqs.question: I have read about Candida auris in New York. Is that the same as a vaginal yeast infection?
faqs.answer: No. The New York City Health Department describes Candida auris as a drug-resistant germ that spreads in hospitals and nursing homes, usually in patients admitted there for another reason, who often have other serious medical conditions. It says there is no known risk to the public and no need for healthy people to be tested. Most vaginal yeast infections are caused by Candida albicans.

tinea-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Most ringworm, athlete's foot and jock itch still clears with standard antifungal treatment, but New York City is where the first U.S. cases of Trichophyton indotineae were found, including a patient with no recent travel, which points to local spread (CDC MMWR, May 2023). That strain is frequently resistant to terbinafine. In 2024 the CDC also reported a sexually transmitted ringworm strain, T. mentagrophytes genotype VII, in four New York City men. If a rash keeps spreading or comes back after a full course of treatment, it needs a fungal culture rather than another round of the same cream. Flat $79 for adults physically in New York.

sectionNotes.what-is: New York's own public health laboratory is part of the resistant ringworm story. In 2023 the state Department of Health reported that testing at its Wadsworth Center identified Trichophyton indotineae, an antifungal-resistant fungus not previously known to be in the United States, in two severe New York City cases. The same year the CDC designated the Wadsworth Center mycology laboratory a reference laboratory for emerging and drug-resistant dermatophytes, and the laboratory reports terbinafine resistance in over 50 percent of T. indotineae isolates.
sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Travel history matters for widespread ringworm in New York. In a 2024 JAMA Dermatology case series of 11 patients with T. indotineae from six New York City medical centers, nine reported previous travel to Bangladesh, and the authors concluded the infections were likely acquired there. The CDC's 2023 report from New York City links that strain's spread in South Asia to misuse and overuse of topical antifungals and corticosteroids, including widely available combination creams.
sectionNotes.differential: The sexually transmitted ringworm strain reported in New York City in 2024, Trichophyton mentagrophytes genotype VII, can cause itchy, ring-shaped, scaly patches on the trunk, groin, genitals or face, and the CDC notes it might be mistaken for eczema or psoriasis. A ring-shaped rash in the groin or genital area that started after a new sexual partner, or one on the face, needs that possibility considered rather than a standard jock itch label.
sectionNotes.treatment-options: Resistant New York cases have needed long courses of oral medicine. In the CDC's 2023 New York City report, one patient's rash did not improve after four weeks of oral terbinafine, another cleared after four weeks of itraconazole, and the report notes that itraconazole can take up to 12 weeks. The 2024 report on the sexually transmitted strain says some patients need oral therapy for up to 3 months. TeleDirectMD does not prescribe oral terbinafine or itraconazole, so a suspected resistant infection is referred for in-person testing and treatment.
sectionNotes.home-care: For the sexually transmitted ringworm strain seen in New York City, the CDC advises avoiding skin-to-skin contact with affected areas and not sharing personal items until symptoms resolve.
sectionNotes.when-not: Some New York ringworm needs testing that a video visit cannot provide. The CDC's 2023 report says providers should consider T. indotineae in patients with widespread tinea, that culture-based identification typically misidentifies it, that correct identification requires genomic sequencing, and that providers should contact their state or local health department for help with testing. Widespread rash, a rash that returns after a full course, or a rash after recent travel to South Asia should be seen in person, ideally by a dermatologist.

faqs.question: Is drug-resistant ringworm common in New York?
faqs.answer: Most ringworm, athlete's foot and jock itch in New York still responds to standard treatment. Resistant strains are a real but smaller problem. The state's Wadsworth Center laboratory, a CDC reference laboratory for drug-resistant dermatophytes since 2023, reports terbinafine resistance in over 50 percent of Trichophyton indotineae isolates, and a 2024 series described 11 patients with that strain at six New York City medical centers.

faqs.question: Can ringworm be passed through sex in New York?
faqs.answer: Yes. In 2024 the CDC reported Trichophyton mentagrophytes genotype VII, a ringworm strain spread through sex, in New York City. It causes itchy, ring-shaped, scaly patches on the trunk, groin, genitals or face and can be mistaken for eczema or psoriasis. Some patients need oral antifungal treatment for up to 3 months, which needs in-person care. Avoid skin-to-skin contact with the rash and do not share personal items until it clears.

faqs.question: I traveled to South Asia and now have a spreading ringworm rash. Can a video visit help?
faqs.answer: A video visit can review the rash and travel history and point you to the right care, but a spreading rash after recent travel to South Asia should be seen in person. In a 2024 series of 11 New York City patients with resistant Trichophyton indotineae, nine had traveled to Bangladesh. Identifying that strain requires laboratory testing, and treatment often means weeks of oral terbinafine or itraconazole, which TeleDirectMD does not prescribe.

hypertension-refills-online.stateConditionParagraph: About 4.2 million adults in New York State, 32.9 percent, have been told they have high blood pressure, and 77.6 percent of them take medicine for it. Among adults without health coverage, only 45.6 percent do (NYS Department of Health, BRFSS Brief 2026-02, 2024 data). A gap in refills is one of the ways blood pressure control slips. A video visit for adults physically in New York can review your home readings, renew a stable regimen and send it electronically to the pharmacy you choose, at a flat $79 with no insurance needed. New York City also requires chain restaurants to flag menu items with 2,300 mg of sodium or more, the first U.S. city to do so.

sectionNotes.what-is: New York's 2024 survey data show that high blood pressure is a little less common in New York City than in the rest of the state: 31.2 percent of city adults report a diagnosis, compared with 34.0 percent elsewhere in New York. Treatment rates are close: among adults with the diagnosis, 76.5 percent in the city take medicine for it, against 78.3 percent in the rest of the state, and men are less likely than women to be on treatment (73.1 versus 82.7 percent).
sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: The same state survey shows how closely blood pressure tracks weight and blood sugar. Among New York adults with obesity, 44.5 percent reported high blood pressure, more than twice the 21.5 percent among adults with neither obesity nor overweight, and 66.1 percent of adults with diabetes reported it. If you live with either condition, a refill visit is a good time to confirm when your potassium and creatinine were last checked, since a basic metabolic panel from the last 12 months is part of the refill lab rule.
sectionNotes.medications: Keep an exact record of what you take. Under New York Education Law Section 6810, a pharmacy must give you a copy of any prescription that is not for a controlled substance when you ask, although the copy is worded as being for information only. A copy, or clear photos of your bottle labels, lets the physician confirm the name, strength and dose of each blood pressure medicine before deciding whether to renew it.
sectionNotes.home-care: If you eat out in New York City, know the limits of the menu sodium warning. The rule, passed unanimously by the city Board of Health on September 9, 2015, applies only to restaurants with 15 or more locations nationwide, so a salty dish at a smaller restaurant carries no icon. The Health Department notes that most sodium comes from processed foods sold in stores and from restaurant food, and that heart disease is the leading cause of death in New York City.

faqs.question: My New York pharmacy is out of my blood pressure medicine. Do I need a new prescription?
faqs.answer: Often not, if the prescription was sent electronically and has not been filled. Under New York Education Law Section 6810, at your request a pharmacy may immediately transfer or forward an unfilled electronic prescription to another pharmacy you name. Call the first pharmacy and give it the name and location of the second one, so you do not go without doses while the stock problem is sorted out.

cat-bite-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Cat bites carry a higher infection risk than most people expect, and in New York they also raise a rabies question. The state Department of Health reports that among domestic animals, cats are the ones most often diagnosed with rabies in New York, rabid animals have been found in every county, and the Wadsworth Center confirmed rabies in 313 animals in 2025. The Department advises reporting every animal bite to your county health department, which arranges a 10-day observation of a healthy cat and helps decide whether rabies treatment is needed; in New York City, the Health Department's online Report an Animal Bite form says any animal bite must be reported within 24 hours. A video visit for adults physically in New York covers wound care, antibiotics when appropriate and that rabies decision. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.how-it-works: A cat bite in New York is also a public health report. In New York City, the Health Code lists animal bites as a reportable condition, physicians must report them to the Health Department within 24 hours, and the person bitten and the cat's owner must also notify the Department. Outside the city, the State Sanitary Code has a physician report a patient's exposure to an animal the physician suspects of rabies to the local health authority, and an adult with no clinician involved reports their own exposure. Before the visit, note where the bite happened and, if you know them, the owner's name and contact details.
sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Rabies in cats is rare in New York City but not absent. The city Health Department counted 22 animals that tested positive for rabies in 2025, almost all raccoons, plus one bat and one cat on Staten Island. Three people received rabies post-exposure treatment after contact with that rabid kitten: two in the home of the rescued stray and a staff member at the veterinary hospital that treated it. A bite or scratch from a stray, feral or newly rescued cat carries a different rabies question than a bite from a vaccinated pet.
sectionNotes.telehealth-eligibility: The checklist asks whether the bite came from a known domestic cat, and in New York a known cat should have a rabies vaccine record. Public Health Law Section 2141 says every cat in the state must be vaccinated against rabies, with limited exemptions, with the first shot no later than four months of age and a second within a year. Under the State Sanitary Code, a cat's owner must show proof of rabies vaccination to the local health officer whenever the cat bites a person; if the owner cannot, the health officer can order the cat confined and observed for 10 days.
sectionNotes.treatment-options: If rabies treatment is needed, it is given in person: the state Department of Health describes it as one dose of human rabies immune globulin and four doses of rabies vaccine. The State Sanitary Code has the treating clinician notify the local health authority before starting that treatment, unless waiting would harm the patient. Outside New York City, Public Health Law Section 2145 makes the county health authority responsible for authorized rabies post-exposure treatment, with insurance applied first; you may also choose your own provider at your own expense. Those county provisions do not apply in New York City.
sectionNotes.home-care: The state Department of Health's first steps after any animal bite are to wash the wound thoroughly with soap and water and to seek medical attention right away. If the health department places the cat under a 10-day confinement, the State Sanitary Code puts the cost on the owner and lets the department set the conditions, which can include the owner keeping the cat. If the cat shows signs of rabies during those 10 days, it is euthanized and tested at a state-approved laboratory.
sectionNotes.when-not: Bites from a stray, feral or unknown cat go to in-person care and your health department, not a video visit. New York City takes animal bite reports through its online Report an Animal Bite form, which says any type of animal bite must be reported within 24 hours. Outside the city, call your county health department. The state rule counts any penetration of skin by an animal's teeth as a bite exposure, so a small puncture still counts.

faqs.question: Do I have to report a cat bite in New York?
faqs.answer: In New York City, yes. The city Health Code requires the person bitten, the cat's owner and anyone else who knows of the bite to notify the Health Department, and its online report form asks for any animal bite within 24 hours. Physicians report bites in the city too. Outside New York City, the State Sanitary Code has an adult who is not under a clinician's care report their own rabies exposure, and the state Department of Health asks people to report all animal bites to the county health department.

faqs.question: What happens to the cat after it bites someone in New York?
faqs.answer: The owner must show the local health officer proof that the cat has had its rabies vaccine. Whether or not it is vaccinated, the local health authority can order the cat confined for 10 days, at the owner's expense, under conditions the authority sets. If the cat shows signs of rabies during that time, it is euthanized and tested at a state-approved laboratory. A cat whose owner cannot be found may also be confined or tested.

faqs.question: Who pays for rabies shots after a cat bite in New York?
faqs.answer: Outside New York City, Public Health Law Section 2145 makes the county health authority responsible for the cost of authorized rabies post-exposure treatment, after any insurance or other third-party coverage is applied. You can instead be treated by a provider of your choice at your own expense without county approval. Section 2146 says these county provisions do not apply to New York City. Rabies shots are given in person, not by video.

trichomoniasis-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Since January 1, 2020, New York's expedited partner therapy law, Public Health Law Section 2312, has covered sexually transmitted infections for which the CDC recommends expedited treatment, and the state Department of Health lists trichomoniasis alongside chlamydia and gonorrhea. Before that change, New York allowed it for chlamydia only. It lets a clinician provide treatment for a patient's sex partner without a separate exam; whether it fits your situation is decided during the visit. A video visit for adults physically in New York can prescribe treatment when appropriate, send it electronically to the pharmacy you choose and plan retesting. Flat $79, discreet.

sectionNotes.what-is: The New York State Department of Health calls trichomoniasis the number one cause of vaginal infections spread through sex, and notes that many people with it have no symptoms and so never get treated. The New York City Health Department describes it as a parasitic infection that makes it more likely to get or spread HIV. Unlike chlamydia, gonorrhea and syphilis, trichomoniasis is not on New York's list of reportable diseases.
sectionNotes.treatment-options: New York's expedited partner therapy law covers trichomoniasis. The state AIDS Institute's guidance lists the partner regimens: for a female partner, the same 7-day metronidazole course or single-dose tinidazole used for patients, and for a male partner, single-dose metronidazole. It allows EPT to be prescribed while syphilis test results are pending or when testing is not possible, such as at a symptomatic telehealth visit. The prescription can be marked "EPT" and filled without the partner's name, the partner pays for it, and in New York City the clinician must also give you written partner materials to pass on.
sectionNotes.home-care: New York's EPT guidance asks both you and your partners to avoid sex without condoms or other barrier protection for at least 7 days after treatment ends, to lower the chance of reinfection. The New York City Health Department advises telling every partner from the previous two months, and getting retested three to four months after treatment to make sure the infection has cleared.
sectionNotes.how-it-works: If you have not been tested yet, the New York City Health Department notes that the test is a vaginal swab, collected by a clinician. Its Sexual Health Clinics provide low- or no-cost STI services to anyone 12 or older, regardless of immigration status, including people who cannot pay the sliding-scale fee. Outside the city, the state Department of Health points people to its Provider Directory to find an STI provider.
sectionNotes.when-not: If a video visit is not the right fit, for example in pregnancy, after a treatment failure or when you need a gonorrhea injection, New York City's Sexual Health Clinics see most patients on a walk-in basis, and the clinic hotline, 347-396-7959, answers Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Outside the city, the state Department of Health's Provider Directory can help you find STI care near you.

faqs.question: Can my partner get trichomoniasis treatment in New York without a visit?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. New York allows expedited partner therapy for trichomoniasis under Public Health Law Section 2312. Your clinician may be able to give you a prescription for your partner that a pharmacist can fill even without your partner's name, and your partner pays for the medicine. New York's guidance says partners should still see a clinician first if they are pregnant or could be, are allergic to antibiotics, take other medicines, or have pain or fever.

faqs.question: Is trichomoniasis reported to the health department in New York?
faqs.answer: No. New York's list of reportable communicable diseases (10 NYCRR Section 2.1) includes chlamydia, gonorrhea and syphilis but not trichomoniasis. The state's Partner Services program follows up reportable STIs such as chlamydia, gonorrhea, syphilis, mpox and HIV. The New York City Health Department advises telling all partners from the previous two months yourself, and expedited partner therapy can get them treated.

faqs.question: Should I get an HIV test after a trichomoniasis diagnosis?
faqs.answer: The New York City Health Department notes that trichomoniasis makes it more likely to get or spread HIV, and New York's EPT guidance recommends that partners get a complete STI check, including an HIV test. In the city, the Health Department's Express Clinics in Chelsea and Fort Greene test people without symptoms for HIV, chlamydia, gonorrhea and syphilis, with HIV results given on site.

bv-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Bacterial vaginosis often comes back: the New York State Department of Health AIDS Institute notes that more than half of people have a recurrence within 6 months. In a 2025 randomized trial in the New England Journal of Medicine, treating the ongoing male partner with oral metronidazole plus clindamycin cream applied to the penis cut recurrence within 12 weeks from 63 percent to 35 percent. The AIDS Institute's February 2026 guidance supports offering this treatment to ongoing partners, while the CDC's 2021 treatment guidelines still do not recommend routine partner treatment. BV is not eligible for expedited partner therapy in New York, so a partner needs a separate visit. In New York City, all Health Department Sexual Health Clinics now offer BV partner treatment, mostly walk-in, regardless of immigration status. A video visit for adult women physically in New York can evaluate symptoms and prescribe treatment when appropriate. Flat $79, discreet.

sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: New York's AIDS Institute guidance, published February 19, 2026, asks clinicians to explain BV a little differently than before. The bacteria behind BV's discharge and odor can also be carried, without symptoms, on the penis or in the vagina of a regular partner. The guidance stresses that this means partners sharing the body's own bacteria, not catching an outside infection such as gonorrhea or syphilis. It links recurrent BV to an ongoing sexual partnership, not using condoms, having an IUD and having an uncircumcised partner.
sectionNotes.treatment-options: The AIDS Institute guidance aims partner treatment at existing, ongoing partners with a penis; it sees no reason to treat past partners. It notes that the supporting trial enrolled monogamous couples, so there are no data for multiple partners, though treating every ongoing partner the same way would be prudent. For a partner with a vagina there are also no data; that partner can be tested for BV and, if treated, needs only standard BV treatment. A male partner needs his own visit with a clinician, in person or by telehealth.
sectionNotes.medications: If your partner is prescribed clindamycin 2% cream for the penis, expect a possible question at the pharmacy. The AIDS Institute notes that in the United States this cream is sold only for vaginal use, with an applicator, and some pharmacists question or refuse prescriptions written for use on the penis. It advises that the prescription say no vaginal applicators are needed, and notes it may help to acknowledge the off-label use. Two major drug references added this use in August 2025.
sectionNotes.home-care: When an ongoing partner is also being treated, the AIDS Institute advises that both of you avoid sex until you have each finished your full course. If you do have sex before then, use condoms, but know that clindamycin cream may weaken condoms, whether it is used in the vagina or, as in partner treatment, on the penis.
sectionNotes.when-not: If you need an in-person exam or testing in New York City, the Health Department's Sexual Health Clinic Hotline, 347-396-7959, also connects callers to a clinic provider by telemedicine for some services, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Adults 19 and older are asked to use insurance or pay a sliding-scale fee based on family size and income, with no proof required and no payment taken at the clinic, and services are provided even if you cannot pay.

faqs.question: Can my male partner get BV partner treatment by telehealth in New York?
faqs.answer: Yes, according to New York's AIDS Institute guidance. Because BV is not eligible for expedited partner therapy in New York, a male partner needs his own visit with a clinician, and the guidance says that visit can be in person or by telehealth. The clinician takes a sexual history, confirms he is an ongoing partner, explains why partner treatment helps prevent recurrence, and offers HIV and STI screening as indicated.

faqs.question: Should my female partner be treated for BV too?
faqs.answer: There are no data on treating female partners, according to New York's AIDS Institute guidance. An ongoing partner with a vagina can be tested for BV using standard methods. If BV is found, or if the two of you and a clinician decide to treat without symptoms, standard BV treatment is used, without the oral-plus-cream combination used for male partners. Past partners who are no longer ongoing do not need treatment.

genital-herpes-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Genital herpes is far more common than most people realize. In a New York City blood-test survey, nearly 28 percent of adults had HSV-2, and 88.4 percent of them did not know it (NYC Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2004 data, published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases, 2008). That is why a first outbreak often comes as a surprise. A video visit for adults physically in New York can assess a first or recurrent outbreak, prescribe antiviral treatment or suppressive therapy when appropriate and send it electronically to the pharmacy you choose. Flat $79, discreet.

sectionNotes.how-it-works: If you want a lab-confirmed diagnosis, the New York City Health Department explains that a clinician may swab or scrape a blister or sore to test for herpes. Blood testing for herpes is possible, the Department notes, but it is not standard practice. A swab needs an in-person visit while a blister or sore is there to sample.
sectionNotes.differential: A new genital sore in New York can also be syphilis, which needs a blood test and in-person care. The state Department of Health reports that primary and secondary syphilis diagnoses fell 18 percent in 2024, to 2,360, and that the rate among females fell to 3.6 per 100,000. In 2023 that rate had been 4.5 per 100,000, nine times the 2014 rate. In New York City, the primary and secondary syphilis rate fell 16.3 percent from 2023 to 2024.
sectionNotes.home-care: The New York City Health Department says condoms and dental dams help prevent the spread of herpes only if they cover the infected area, and advises avoiding sex while an open sore is present. The state Department of Health adds that herpes can pass through skin a condom does not cover. The city gives out free condoms through the NYC Condom Availability Program, with distribution sites listed on the NYC Health Map.
sectionNotes.when-not: Pregnancy changes the plan. The New York City Health Department warns that herpes is dangerous for babies when a pregnant parent is newly infected late in pregnancy, that it can cause serious infections, brain damage or death in newborns, and that a cesarean section is recommended if sores are present at delivery. If you are pregnant and you or your partner has herpes, tell your prenatal care provider; the Department notes that medicine can lower the risk of an outbreak at delivery.

faqs.question: Is genital herpes reported to the health department in New York?
faqs.answer: Not in adults. New York's list of reportable communicable diseases (10 NYCRR Section 2.1) includes herpes only in infants 60 days old or younger, and the New York City Health Code likewise requires reporting of neonatal herpes. Adult genital herpes is not on either list. The state says its Partner Services staff follow up reportable infections such as chlamydia, gonorrhea, syphilis, mpox and HIV.

faqs.question: Where can I get tested for herpes in New York City?
faqs.answer: The New York City Health Department's Sexual Health Clinics provide low- or no-cost STI services to anyone 12 or older, regardless of immigration status, mostly on a walk-in basis. Test results can take up to seven to ten days. Testing is usually done by swabbing a blister or sore, so go while one is present. The clinic hotline, 347-396-7959, answers Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

acid-reflux-refills-online.stateConditionParagraph: A refill visit for acid reflux is also a check for warning signs. The American College of Gastroenterology recommends endoscopy for reflux with trouble swallowing, weight loss, bleeding, vomiting or anemia, and advises taking a proton pump inhibitor at the lowest dose that controls symptoms. Esophageal cancer is uncommon but serious, which is why those warning signs are checked first. For adults physically in New York whose symptoms are stable, a video visit can review your current medicine, screen for those signs and renew it when appropriate. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Smoking, one of the reflux triggers listed above, is a habit New York tracks closely. About 1.4 million adult New Yorkers, 9.3 percent, smoked cigarettes in 2023, according to the state Department of Health, and New York City's adult smoking rate was 8 percent that year. The reason to quit goes beyond heartburn: the state's cancer data group esophageal cancer with lung, larynx and oral cavity cancers as the four cancers most closely related to tobacco.
sectionNotes.symptoms-redflags: The warning signs in this table matter because esophageal cancer, while uncommon, is serious. The state's data also show esophageal cancer incidence declining steeply since 2006 in both New York City and the rest of the state, and the state's 2018 to 2022 data show esophageal cancer diagnosed more often in men than in women.
sectionNotes.home-care: If you smoke and want to quit, the New York State Smokers' Quitline, 866-NY-QUITS (866-697-8487), lets you apply for a free starter kit of nicotine medications, including patches and lozenges that most adults are eligible to receive, and talk with a quit coach.

faqs.question: Can a New York pharmacy mail my PPI refills without asking me?
faqs.answer: No. Under New York Education Law Section 6810, a pharmacy registered with the state, including a registered out-of-state pharmacy, may not deliver a new or refilled prescription off premises without your consent. A pharmacy that delivers without consent must accept the return and credit you for any charges you paid. Refill reminder and medication adherence programs are still allowed, so you can keep reminders while choosing pickup.

cold-sore-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Cold sores are caused by herpes simplex virus, usually type 1, and the infection is common: in the CDC's national survey for 2015 to 2016, 47.8 percent of Americans aged 14 to 49 had HSV-1 antibodies. Antibodies show infection, not how often cold sores appear. For many people a cold sore clears on its own in 7 to 14 days, and treatment started early can ease discomfort and speed healing, per the American Academy of Dermatology. A sore near the eye, or an eye that becomes painful or light sensitive, needs an eye doctor right away. A video visit for adults physically in New York can decide whether an antiviral is appropriate. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.home-care: If sun brings on your cold sores, the American Academy of Dermatology says that wearing a broad-spectrum lip balm with SPF 30 or higher year-round may help prevent new ones.
sectionNotes.differential: A sore on the genitals is a different question from a cold sore on the lip, even though the same virus can cause both: the CDC reports that an increasing proportion of anogenital herpes infections are caused by HSV-1, especially among young women and men who have sex with men. TeleDirectMD has a separate genital herpes visit. In New York City, the Health Department's Sexual Health Clinics also offer walk-in evaluation of STI symptoms at low or no cost to anyone 12 or older, regardless of immigration status.

faqs.question: Can the cold sore virus cause genital herpes, and where can I get checked in New York City?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cold sores are usually caused by HSV-1, and the CDC reports that a growing share of genital herpes infections are caused by HSV-1 as well. A video visit can review genital symptoms on TeleDirectMD's genital herpes page. In New York City, the Health Department's Sexual Health Clinics offer walk-in, low- to no-cost evaluation for signs and symptoms of STIs to anyone 12 or older, regardless of immigration status.

dandruff-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Scalp seborrheic dermatitis often flares when the weather turns cold and dry, according to the American Academy of Dermatology, which lists zinc pyrithione, salicylic acid, sulfur, selenium sulfide, ketoconazole and coal tar as dandruff shampoo ingredients to look for. When over-the-counter products are not enough, a video visit for adults physically in New York can look at the scalp on camera and decide whether a prescription shampoo or other treatment is appropriate. If a prescription shampoo is prescribed, New York law (Education Law Sections 6810 and 6816-a) has the pharmacist fill it with a less expensive generic on the state's approved list unless the prescriber marks it dispense as written. Dandruff that persists or is severe deserves a dermatologist's evaluation. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Severe seborrheic dermatitis in an adult can be a reason to check HIV status, since the condition is far more common in people with HIV. New York's Public Health Law Section 2781-a requires an HIV test to be offered to everyone 13 and older who receives primary care from a physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner or midwife, unless one has already been offered or done, and a test is still offered when otherwise indicated. In New York City, the Health Department's Sexual Health Clinics provide confidential, low- to no-cost HIV testing to anyone 12 or older, regardless of immigration status.

faqs.question: Why might HIV testing come up for bad dandruff in New York?
