faqs.answer: Seborrheic dermatitis, the condition behind most dandruff, is much more common and more severe in people with HIV, so a severe or sudden flare in an adult can be a reason to test. New York law separately requires primary care clinicians to offer HIV testing to everyone 13 and older unless it has already been offered or done. In New York City, the Health Department's Sexual Health Clinics offer confidential, low- to no-cost testing.

ear-pain-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: A video visit cannot look at the eardrum; that takes an otoscope, in person. A visit can sort out whether your symptoms fit swimmer's ear, an ear canal infection that, per the American Academy of Otolaryngology, occurs when water stays trapped in the canal, and treat it with ear drops when appropriate. In New York City, a combined sewer overflow advisory is issued when heavy rain or snow spills untreated sewage into the waters around New York Harbor, water that may carry illness-causing bacteria. Severe pain with fever and swelling behind the ear, facial weakness or sudden hearing loss needs in-person care. Flat $79 for adults physically in New York.

sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Swimming water anywhere in New York can carry germs into the ear. The state Department of Health warns that germs in swimming water can enter your body through your mouth, eyes, ears and nose, and that levels of fecal contamination can be higher after heavy rains. Public bathing beaches in the state are regulated under Subpart 6-2 of the State Sanitary Code, permitted and inspected by local health departments, and are closed or have swimming advisories posted when the beach is unsafe. Outside a regulated beach, the Department advises assuming that all waters have fecal contamination even if you can't see it.
sectionNotes.symptoms-redflags: Diabetes is common in New York: the state Department of Health estimates that 1.7 million adult New Yorkers, 10.6 percent, had diagnosed diabetes in 2023. That matters for ear pain because, as the list above notes, diabetes raises the risk of severe and necrotizing otitis externa, which needs urgent in-person care. If you have diabetes or a weakened immune system and your ear pain is getting worse quickly or the ear is draining, skip the video visit and get seen in person.
sectionNotes.home-care: Once your ear has healed, checking the water before you swim can help you avoid the next infection. In 2025 the NYC Health Department routinely monitored water quality at 24 permitted beaches, and when rainfall exceeds a set threshold for a beach, it issues a water quality advisory for a set period. You can see each beach's status on the Health Department's Beach Water Quality map or by calling 311, and you can report a swimming-related illness through 311.
sectionNotes.medications: Two New York pharmacy rules can help with the cost of prescription ear drops. Under Education Law Section 6816-a, a pharmacist substitutes a less expensive drug product with the same active ingredients, dosage form and strength as the drug prescribed, when the substitute is on the state's approved list and the prescriber does not prohibit substitution. Every New York pharmacy that sells drugs at retail must also make a drug retail price list available and display a sign reading "Drug Retail Price List Available Upon Request."

faqs.question: Is it safe to swim at a New York City beach after it rains?
faqs.answer: Check first. The NYC Health Department uses rainfall thresholds to predict when sewer overflows may affect each beach, and when rainfall exceeds a beach's threshold it issues a water quality advisory for a set period. Across the 24 beaches it monitored in 2025, its annual report counts 960 advisory days in total, summed beach by beach, for rainfall, storms and high bacteria readings. The Beach Water Quality map and 311 show current status. Outside the city, the state says fecal contamination can be higher after heavy rains.

faqs.question: I have diabetes and ear pain. Can I use a video visit in New York?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but not when symptoms are worsening fast. More than 1 in 10 adult New Yorkers has diagnosed diabetes, according to the state Department of Health, and diabetes raises the risk of necrotizing otitis externa, a severe ear canal infection that needs urgent in-person care. If you have diabetes and rapidly worsening ear pain or drainage, get seen in person. For milder, stable symptoms, Dr. Bhavsar can assess by video whether in-person care is needed.

eczema-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: In New York City, heat season runs from October 1 to May 31: landlords must keep apartments at 68 degrees or warmer by day when it is below 55 outside, and 62 or warmer overnight. That means months of cold air outside and heated rooms inside. The American Academy of Dermatology notes that cold can dry the skin and that sweating from overheating can also trigger flares, and advises moisturizing after bathing. A video visit for adults physically in New York can review a flare on camera and adjust treatment when appropriate. Fever, pus, golden crusts or a rash that spreads rapidly needs in-person care. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Work can be the trigger. New York runs what the state Department of Health calls the nation's only state-based occupational health clinic network. Under the state Workers' Compensation Board's definition, an occupational disease is any illness or condition associated with a particular occupation or industry, so a rash caused by gloves, wet work or chemicals on the job can fall under it.
sectionNotes.differential: In New York, a ring-shaped rash that does not respond to eczema treatment deserves a second look for fungus. The CDC's 2024 report on a sexually transmitted ringworm strain in New York City notes it might be mistaken for eczema or psoriasis, and the CDC's 2023 report on resistant Trichophyton indotineae, first found in the city, links that strain's spread to misuse of topical steroids and steroid-antifungal combination creams. Putting a steroid on an undiagnosed fungal rash can make it harder to recognize and treat.
sectionNotes.home-care: Hot water is a known eczema trigger, and New York City buildings run hot. Under the city's housing rules, landlords must supply hot water 365 days a year at a constant minimum of 120 degrees Fahrenheit. Let the shower mix down to lukewarm, keep it short, and apply moisturizer while your skin is still damp. If your building has no hot water at all, contact your landlord first and then 311.
sectionNotes.when-not: If your rash started or worsens at work, or you suspect a chemical, glove or other job exposure, the state's Occupational Health Clinic Network can evaluate work-related illness. Its clinics are available to all workers, retirees and residents in New York State, they can bill most major insurers, and the Department of Health says no worker will be turned away because of an inability to pay.

faqs.question: Could my eczema be caused by my job in New York?
faqs.answer: It can, and it is worth asking if the rash is worst on your hands or eases on days off. New York's Workers' Compensation Board defines an occupational disease as any illness or condition associated with a particular occupation or industry, and claims must be filed within two years of the disability or of when you knew, or should have known, it was caused by work. The state's Occupational Health Clinic Network evaluates work-related illness and turns no worker away for inability to pay.

faqs.question: My eczema cream isn't working. Could it be ringworm instead?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. In New York City, the CDC has reported a sexually transmitted ringworm strain that might be mistaken for eczema or psoriasis, and a resistant strain whose spread is linked to steroid and steroid-antifungal combination creams. A ring-shaped patch with a raised, scaly edge, a rash that spreads despite steroid cream, or a rash after a new sexual partner should be looked at for fungus, sometimes with a skin scraping in person.

erectile-dysfunction-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Erectile dysfunction can be a symptom of another health problem. The NIH lists diabetes and heart and blood vessel diseases, such as high blood pressure, among the most common causes, and an estimated 1.7 million adult New Yorkers, 10.6 percent, have diagnosed diabetes (state Department of Health, 2023 data). A video visit for adult men physically in New York starts with your health history and medicines. The FDA label for sildenafil says it must not be used with nitrates, and chest pain, dizziness or nausea during sex calls for medical help right away. When treatment is appropriate, it is sent electronically to the pharmacy you choose. Flat $79, discreet.

sectionNotes.causes-risk-factors: Newer state data update the diabetes picture: about 1.7 million adult New Yorkers, 10.6 percent, had diagnosed diabetes in 2023, and the rate among men was 11.5 percent (state Department of Health, October 2025). High blood pressure is also common among New York men, at 35.7 percent in 2024, and only 73.1 percent of men with that diagnosis take medicine for it. Both conditions can contribute to erectile dysfunction, so an ED visit is also a chance to ask whether yours are under control.
sectionNotes.symptoms-redflags: If erectile problems come with low mood, hopelessness or thoughts of suicide, that needs attention before any prescription. In New York, calling or texting 988, or chatting online, reaches trained crisis counselors 24/7, free and confidential, and the state has dedicated 988 contact centers for people in a mental health crisis. If you are in immediate danger, call 911.
sectionNotes.when-not: Poppers are recreational alkyl nitrites and must never be combined with ED medicine. The New York City Health Department warns that poppers are sold as deodorizers, solvent cleaners or nail polish removers in small bottles that can look like energy drinks, and that swallowing them can cause methemoglobinemia, a type of blood poisoning. If someone feels sick from poppers, the NYC Poison Center answers 24/7 at 212-POISONS (212-764-7667), free and confidential. Call 911 if the person is unconscious, having seizures or having trouble breathing.
sectionNotes.home-care: Stopping smoking is one of the lifestyle steps above, and New York offers free help with it. Through the New York State Smokers' Quitline, 866-NY-QUITS (866-697-8487), adults can apply for a free starter kit of nicotine medications, such as patches and lozenges, and talk with a quit coach. About 1.4 million adult New Yorkers still smoked cigarettes in 2023.

faqs.question: Is it safe to order ED medication from a website that ships to New York?
faqs.answer: Check that a real pharmacy is behind it. New York requires any pharmacy outside the state that ships prescription drugs to patients here, including internet pharmacies, to register with the State Education Department (Education Law Section 6808-b). Registered nonresident pharmacies must offer a toll-free line to a pharmacist at least 40 hours a week and print it on every container.

faqs.question: If an out-of-state mail-order pharmacy fills my New York prescription, whose rules apply?
faqs.answer: Largely that pharmacy's home state. A registered nonresident pharmacy must stay licensed and in good standing where it is located and follow that state's rules for drugs it ships into New York (Education Law Section 6808-b). If you choose an out-of-state dispenser, that state's generic substitution law applies (Section 6816-a). New York law still requires your consent before a registered pharmacy delivers a new or refilled prescription.

hair-loss-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Treating male pattern hair loss is long term: the FDA label for finasteride notes that stopping it reverses the effect within 12 months. Under New York Education Law Section 6826, every pharmacy must give you its retail price list for the 150 most frequently prescribed drugs on request, updated at least weekly. A video visit for adults physically in New York can assess the pattern and discuss options when appropriate. Finasteride is approved for men only, and a woman who is or may be pregnant should not handle crushed or broken tablets. Patchy bald spots, hair falling out in clumps, or a burning, tender scalp need in-person care. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.differential: Patchy hair loss has one cause worth knowing about in New York: secondary syphilis. The CDC lists patchy hair loss among its symptoms, along with a rash that can appear on the palms or the soles of the feet. The New York City Health Department counted 1,273 primary and secondary syphilis cases among men in 2024, while the rate fell 16.3 percent from 2023. Patchy loss, with or without a rash, needs an in-person exam and testing, not a hair loss prescription.
sectionNotes.medications: Generic finasteride and brand-name Propecia contain the same active ingredient. New York law requires the prescriber to tell you whether a brand name or its generic equivalent was prescribed (Education Law Section 6810), and a pharmacist may substitute an approved generic unless the prescriber marks the prescription dispense as written, by hand or with an electronic direction. If you have a reason to want the brand, raise it during the visit so the choice is made on purpose.
sectionNotes.treatment-options: Hair loss treatment is heavily marketed online. If a website ships finasteride to you in New York, the pharmacy filling it must be registered with the New York State Education Department even when it is located in another state, and internet pharmacies are expressly included (Education Law Section 6808-b). A registered out-of-state pharmacy must also print a toll-free number for reaching one of its pharmacists on each container, so check the label when your first order arrives.
sectionNotes.home-care: The FDA-approved label for finasteride lists depression and suicidal thoughts among effects reported in general use, so notice how your mood changes after you start it and tell a physician promptly about any change. In New York, calling or texting 988, or chatting online, reaches trained crisis counselors 24/7 at no cost, and the state runs dedicated 988 contact centers. If you are in immediate danger, call 911.

faqs.question: Where can I get tested for syphilis in New York City if my hair loss is patchy?
faqs.answer: The NYC Health Department's Sexual Health Clinics offer syphilis testing and STI treatment at low or no cost, and you can still be seen if you have no insurance or cannot pay the sliding-scale fee. Most clinic services are walk-in, with no appointment. The clinic hotline is 347-396-7959, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Patchy hair loss also needs an in-person exam by a dermatologist or primary care physician.

psoriasis-refills-online.pageTitle: Psoriasis Prescription Refills Online in New York | TeleDirectMD
psoriasis-refills-online.metaDescription: Renew a topical psoriasis prescription by video in New York with a physician, flat $79. Plus how New York step therapy overrides and DFS external appeals work if a plan says no.
psoriasis-refills-online.h1: Psoriasis Prescription Refills Online in New York
psoriasis-refills-online.stateConditionParagraph: If your topical psoriasis prescription is out of refills, note that under Education Law Section 6810, a pharmacy cannot refill a prescription more times than the prescriber authorized, and a new prescription must be sent electronically. A video visit for adults physically in New York with stable, previously diagnosed plaque psoriasis can review your skin and regimen and renew it when appropriate. New joint symptoms call for a fuller evaluation: the American Academy of Dermatology notes that psoriatic arthritis often starts with a few puffy joints, a swollen finger or toe, or morning stiffness, most often 5 to 12 years after psoriasis begins. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.eligibility-checklist: A refill visit starts from an existing diagnosis, and New York law helps you document it. Under Public Health Law Section 18, a clinician who treated you must furnish a copy of your patient information within a reasonable time after a written request, must offer inspection of it within ten days, and may not deny you access solely because you cannot pay.
sectionNotes.how-it-works: New York prescriptions travel electronically, and that helps when a pharmacy is out of your cream or you are away from your usual store. Education Law Section 6810 lets a pharmacy that received an electronic prescription, and has not filled it, forward it immediately to another pharmacy you designate at your request. Ask the first pharmacy to transfer it rather than starting over with a new prescription.
sectionNotes.medications: Psoriasis regimens often come with exact instructions about how thinly to apply, where, and for how many weeks, especially for high-potency steroids. If English is not your first language, Education Law Section 6829 requires any New York pharmacy that is part of a group of eight or more in the state under the same corporate owner to provide free, competent oral interpretation and to translate prescription labels, warning labels and other written material into the pharmacy primary languages for its region. Covered pharmacies must post a notice of this right at the prescription counter.
treatment-options: New York limits how a health plan can make you try other drugs first. New York Insurance Law defines step therapy as a protocol that "establishes the specific sequence in which prescription drugs for a specified medical condition are approved." Under Chapter 512 of the Laws of 2016, effective January 1, 2017, your prescriber can ask the plan for a step therapy override with documentation that, for example, you already tried the required drug under your current or previous coverage and it was stopped for lack of effect or an adverse event, or that you are stable on the drug your clinician chose.

The plan must decide within 72 hours of receiving the supporting documentation, or within 24 hours when your health is in serious jeopardy without the drug, and a missed deadline counts as an override. The law covers insurers and HMOs regulated in New York. It does not apply to self-insured employer plans or Medicare. Your TeleDirectMD visit is a flat $79 self-pay, but if you fill the prescription through your plan's pharmacy benefit, these rules apply to that fill.

faqs.question: How do I get my old psoriasis records in New York?
faqs.answer: Ask the clinician or practice that diagnosed you, in writing. New York Public Health Law Section 18 requires a provider to furnish a copy of your patient information within a reasonable time, to offer inspection within ten days of a written request, and not to deny you access solely because you cannot pay. Records that show the diagnosis and your current topical regimen help a refill visit go smoothly.

faqs.question: My pharmacy is out of my psoriasis medicine. Can the prescription move to another New York pharmacy?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. New York Education Law Section 6810 allows a pharmacy that received an electronic prescription, and has not filled it, to forward it immediately to another pharmacy you choose, at your request. Ask the first pharmacy to transfer it. If you have no refills left, a new prescription is needed, and a video visit can review your skin and regimen and renew it when appropriate.

faqs.question: Can I get my prescription label in my own language in New York?
faqs.answer: At many pharmacies, yes. Education Law Section 6829 requires New York pharmacies that are part of a group of eight or more in the state under the same corporate owner to offer free, competent oral interpretation and translated prescription labels, warning labels and written materials in the main languages of their region, which are set by regulation from Census data, up to seven per region. Ask at the counter.

faqs.question: My New York health plan wants me to try a different psoriasis drug first. Can that be overridden?
faqs.answer: Often, if your prescriber documents a reason. New York's step therapy law, effective January 1, 2017, lets a prescriber request an override when, for example, the required drug is expected to be ineffective given your history, you already tried it and it was stopped for lack of effect or an adverse event, or you are stable on the drug your clinician selected. The plan must decide within 72 hours of receiving the documentation, or 24 hours if your health is in serious jeopardy without the drug. The law does not apply to self-insured employer plans or Medicare.

faqs.question: My New York plan denied my psoriasis medication. Can I appeal outside the plan?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a New York State external appeal. If an insurer or HMO denies care as not medically necessary, experimental or investigational, or out of network, and your internal appeal fails, you can send an application to the Department of Financial Services within 4 months of the plan's final adverse determination. An independent external appeal agent decides, and the decision is binding on you and the plan. Plans may charge $25 per appeal, no more than $75 a plan year, refunded if the denial is overturned and waived if the fee is a hardship. Decisions come within 30 days, or 72 hours when expedited; for a non-formulary drug, 72 hours standard and 24 hours expedited. A denied step therapy override can also be appealed.

scabies-treatment-online.stateConditionParagraph: Scabies spreads through skin-to-skin contact, including sex, and through shared clothing, towels and bedding, according to the New York City Health Department. It advises treating household members, including children, even without symptoms, and examining and treating sex and intimate partners from the past six weeks. The CDC adds that household members and close contacts should be treated at the same time as the person with scabies. Clothing, bedding and towels should be machine washed and dried hot. A video visit for adults physically in New York can review the rash and plan treatment when appropriate. TeleDirectMD treats adults only, so children in the household should be treated at the same time by their own clinician. Thick, crusted skin needs in-person care. Flat $79.

sectionNotes.how-it-works: If you work in New York, the state's paid sick leave law (Labor Law Section 196-b) covers time off for the diagnosis, care or treatment of your own illness or health condition, so time off work for the visit and treatment can come out of that leave. Employers with 5 to 99 workers must provide up to 40 hours of paid sick leave a year, and employers with 100 or more up to 56 hours. Your employer may not require you to disclose confidential information about the condition to approve the leave.
sectionNotes.differential: The New York City Health Department describes how scabies is confirmed in person: mineral oil is applied to the skin, the skin is scraped, and the sample is examined under a microscope. A video visit cannot do that, so if the rash pattern on camera is not typical, or treatment has not worked, an in-person scraping is the next step. The same brochure notes that people do not catch scabies mites from animals and animals do not catch them from people.
sectionNotes.home-care: The New York City Health Department adds two steps to the hot wash and dry. Items that cannot be washed should be sealed in a plastic bag for at least 72 hours, and carpets and upholstered furniture should be vacuumed. It also advises wearing clean clothes, not sharing clothes or towels, and washing bedding and towels often while the household is being treated.
sectionNotes.when-not: One case of scabies caught in everyday life is not a public health report in New York: the state Department of Health says sporadic, community-acquired cases are not reportable. Outbreaks in hospitals, nursing homes and other health care facilities are handled differently. The Department's memo on scabies in health care facilities says outbreaks must be reported to the state, that both symptomatic employees and exposed employees without symptoms should be treated, and that household members and sexual contacts of symptomatic employees must be treated at the same time. If several people where you live or work have the same rash, that needs a facility-wide response, not a single video visit.

faqs.question: Can I go to work with scabies in New York?
faqs.answer: Ask your employer about its own policy. For any job, the state's paid sick leave law covers time for the diagnosis, care and treatment of your own illness, and your employer may not require you to disclose confidential medical information to grant that leave.

faqs.question: Do I have to report scabies to the health department in New York?
faqs.answer: Not for a single case picked up in the community. The New York State Department of Health says sporadic, community-acquired scabies cases are not reportable. Outbreaks in hospitals, nursing homes and other health care facilities are different: the Department's guidance says those must be reported to the state, and the facility handles that. Your household and close contacts still need treatment at the same time as you.

faqs.question: Can I catch scabies from my dog or cat?
faqs.answer: No. The New York City Health Department's scabies brochure says humans are not at risk of contracting scabies mites from an animal, or the other way around. Human scabies spreads through skin-to-skin contact, including sex, and through shared clothing, towels and bedding, so treatment focuses on you and the people you live with or are intimate with.
